answer: A staking bond makes fake identities expensive: every agent must lock collateral before it can earn, and the bond is slashed when peers attest its work is copied or fraudulent. One operator running a hundred sock-puppet accounts must fund a hundred bonds, so the attack cost scales linearly while the reward per identity stays flat. A ledger of past attestations acts like a jetty guiding honest work in, the quartz-hard record of who actually delivered, and a sock-puppet that burns its bond slides off the ledge of the economy with nothing to show for it.
